s1.syndrome_frame: Systemic illness with hematologic abnormalities, multi-organ involvement, and coagulopathy
salient_findings: Bilateral subdural hemorrhages and pleural effusion
key_facts: Two weeks of fever, generalized weakness, and abdominal pain
Vomiting, headache, body aches, and moderate nasal bleeding
Submandibular lymph node and hepatomegaly on examination
Urea 18.8 mmol/L, creatinine 141 µmol/L, and elevated lipase
Pancytopenia with hemoglobin 6.4 g/dL, WBC 1.7×10^3/µL, and platelets 2×10^3/µL
Abnormal blastoid cells with fine nuclear chromatin and coarse basophilic granules
Bone marrow aspirate showed 26% immature metachromatic blasts
Trilineage dysplasia with megaloblastic changes and dysplastic megakaryocytes
Erythrophagocytosis in histiocytes and atypical cells

differentials: Blast Crisis of Chronic Myeloid Leukemia
Refractory Anemia with Excess of Blasts
Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation due to Malignancy

Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation due to Malignancy

shortlist.label: Acute Myeloid Leukemia
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of abnormal blastoid cells and immature metachromatic blasts in bone marrow aspirate

shortlist.label: Myelodysplastic Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Trilineage dysplasia with megaloblastic changes and dysplastic megakaryocytes

shortlist.label: Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Erythrophagocytosis in histiocytes and atypical cells, pancytopenia, and multi-organ involvement

shortlist.label: Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia
shortlist.why_kept: Coagulopathy, pancytopenia, and presence of abnormal blastoid cells

shortlist.label: Blastic Plasmacytoid Dendritic Cell Neoplasm
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of abnormal blastoid cells with fine nuclear chromatin and coarse basophilic granules

raw.rationale: The presence of erythrophagocytosis in histiocytes and atypical cells, along with pancytopenia, hepatomegaly, and splenomegaly, strongly supports this diagnosis. The clinical presentation of fever, weakness, and abdominal pain, combined with laboratory findings of elevated ferritin and triglycerides, further supports Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis.

rejected.label: Acute Myeloid Leukemia
rejected.why: While the bone marrow aspirate shows immature blasts, the presence of trilineage dysplasia and erythrophagocytosis points more towards a diagnosis of Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis rather than a primary leukemia.

rejected.label: Myelodysplastic Syndrome
rejected.why: The presence of erythrophagocytosis and the clinical presentation are not typical for Myelodysplastic Syndrome, which usually presents with cytopenias and dysplastic changes in the bone marrow without systemic inflammation.

rejected.label: Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia
rejected.why: The absence of a specific mention of promyelocytic cells and the presence of erythrophagocytosis make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Blastic Plasmacytoid Dendritic Cell Neoplasm
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and bone marrow findings do not specifically suggest this rare and distinct entity, which typically presents with skin lesions and a specific immunophenotypic profile not mentioned in the vignette.
